(3) Condition B is that, where no prohibition notice has been given (or one was given but
has been withdrawn)—
(a) the court is satisfied on the balance of probabilities that the person is carrying
on, or is likely to carry on, a prohibited activity, and
(b) the court considers that the person would fail to comply with a prohibition
notice if given.

(4) Condition C is that the court considers it necessary and proportionate to make the
prohibition order for the purpose of preventing the person from carrying on any
prohibited activity.

(5) If a court makes a prohibition order under this section based on condition A having
been met, the prohibition notice is to be treated as having been withdrawn.
